description: Designed and built a retrieval-augmented incident knowledge system that indexes past incidents, Slack threads, postmortems, and resolution actions, and attaches the three most similar prior incidents and their fixes to each new page.
Implemented symptom-signature matching using embeddings over alert payloads, error logs, and affected-service metadata, achieving 87% top-3 match accuracy on 150 historical incidents.

Built an ingestion pipeline that captures the actions that resolved an incident (commands run, rollbacks, merged PRs, config changes) rather than only narrative write-ups, turning tribal knowledge into searchable, structured records.
Developed an LLM-based generator that drafts runbooks from recurring resolution patterns, and flags incidents where the fix depended on a single engineer's knowledge.
Integrated with Slack, PagerDuty/Alertmanager webhooks, and a Git provider so context appears inside the on-call workflow without engineers switching tools.
Evaluated the system against 50 replayed incidents, reducing estimated time-to-first-action by 32% and cutting reliance on the most senior responders for repeat incidents.

Built and iterated on a Python-based healthcare RAG application using LangChain, vector embeddings, and LLM APIs, improving clinical-note retrieval relevance by 14% while evaluating usability, response quality, and model behavior.

Preprocessed and curated 500 remote patient-monitoring records with Pandas and scikit-learn, creating structured ML-ready datasets and validation workflows for rapid model experimentation and evaluation.

Evaluated patient-risk model performance using precision, recall, and F1 scores, testing hyperparameter configurations and documenting model limitations, supporting responsible AI evaluation and AI governance considerations.

Partnered with data scientists through 5 iterative development cycles on PyTorch and Hugging Face experiments, contributing to model testing, code reviews, technical discussions, and collaborative AI development.

Designed and built Python automation frameworks to collect, clean, and analyze large-scale datasets from multiple sources, replacing manual research workflows and improving accuracy and repeatability of recurring technology assessments.
Developed modular, maintainable data pipelines following clean-architecture principles, enabling scalable analysis workflows and reuse across future automation projects.
Debugged and optimized pipeline failures end-to-end, performing root-cause analysis on data quality and integration issues to keep recurring assessments reliable.

Partnered with engineering, product, and leadership stakeholders to translate technical findings on AI, XR, and emerging technologies into actionable recommendations and documentation used by executive leadership.

Facilitated and structured engaging tutorials on diverse machine learning topics including supervised, unsupervised, and probabilistic models for 95 students, reinforcing core concepts through hands-on Python coding.

Provided individualized mentoring and project guidance, boosting project completion rates by 20% through effective coaching in Python libraries (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn) and best practices in model development.
Enhanced overall student performance by 15% by delivering detailed, constructive feedback on assignments and exams, while promoting collaborative problem-solving and peer reviews.
Coordinated with faculty to develop comprehensive course materials, optimize assessments, and align learning outcomes to ensure an engaging curriculum.
